articleTitle: A novel method for electret production using impulse voltages
abstract: A novel method for producing electrets is proposed in which an electric discharge is induced by a negative impulse voltage in a small air gap. The dielectric foil to be charged is placed between two planar electrodes, being in contact with one of them and separated from the other by the air gap. The electric discharge in the gap causes electric charges to deposit onto the dielectric surface where they are trapped, thus forming the electret. Measurements carried out with Teflon FEP (fluoroethylene propylene) show a very uniform deposition, and that the sample surface potential increases linearly with increasing impulse peak voltage. In principle, this method compares with the corona discharge for the production of electrets with regard to high turnout and low cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of the corona discharge in different atmospheres on the thermally stimulated charge injection of Teflon FEP
abstract: It was shown previously that negative corona treatment of Teflon FEP decreases the thermal stability of the electrets. Thermally stimulated discharge measurements of treated samples presented, besides the usual peak of 210 degrees C, a new broad current peak in the temperature range of 100 to 160 degrees C. Further investigations were carried out on N/sub 2/, CO/sub 2/, O/sub 2/, and dry air in order to study the effect of the corona atmosphere on the corona treatment. In N/sub 2/ no effect was observed, while for CO/sub 2/ and O/sub 2/ a well-defined current peak appears with a maximum at 120 degrees C. In dry air no significant differences were observed when compared with the results for normal air.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Changes in photo-induced pyroelectric transients during polarization reversal in VDF-TrFE copolymers
abstract: The pyroelectric current transient induced by laser irradiation was measured for VDF/TrFE (vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) copolymers in order to examine the polarization distribution in the thickness direction developed during ferroelectric polarization reversal. It is found that the polarization profile is uniform for the case of relatively fast switching. On the other hand, the slow switching process develops nonuniform polarization profiles, suggesting that polarization reversal progress from the positively biased side.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polar species as charge carrier traps in molecular solids
abstract: The presence of polar impurity species in nonpolar molecular materials may result in the appearance of traps for charge carriers. Calculations of local values of the polarization energy in the vicinity of a dipolar defect carried out on a simple cubic molecular lattice show that traps as deep as several tenths of an electron volt can result in such a way, their depths and cross sections depending on the dipole moments of the guest molecules.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the charge storage and decay mechanism in silicon dioxide
abstract: A mechanism for both the storage and the decay of charge in a charged silicon dioxide layer is proposed. The oxide layer needs neutral traps (NETs) to obtain stable trapped negative charge, after having been charged, resulting in an electret that can be applied in microphones. The hydrolysis of the silanol groups, followed by charge injection, results in an electrochemical reaction with immobile SiO as one of the reaction products. Decay of the stable charge thus obtained can occur by the clustering of water molecules at inner silanol groups, resulting in a conductive hydrogen bonded network, which eventually leads to the discharge of the electret.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Life time of thermal electrets of carnauba wax, esters, fatty acids and alcohols
abstract: Residual surface charge with time was observed with thermal electrets of carnauba wax, esters extracted from carnauba wax, fatty acids and alcohols derived by hydrolysis of esters. All the electrets were prepared in 1951-1953. The samples were poled by applying various electric fields in the temperature range between room temperature and 65 degrees C. After poling, both surfaces of the electrets were shorted with tin foil and kept in a desiccator. Thirty-six years have passed after the preparation of the electrets; a stable homocharge of (4.6 approximately 6.6)*10/sup -5/ C/m/sup 2/ was observed for electrets of carnauba wax, esters, and fatty acids, but no charge was observed for fatty alcohols.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Charge distribution in electron-beam irradiation polymers
abstract: The laser-induced pressure pulse (LIPP) method was used to measure charge distributions in electron-beam charged Teflon, Mylar, and Kapton as a function of charge density. One-side metallized 24 to 25 mu m thick Mylar and Kapton films were charged through their nonmetallized face with 10 to 40 keV electron beams and investigated with the LIPP method. The measurements show negative space-charge layers whose depth increased with electron-beam energy and with injected charge density. In addition, positive surface- and near-surface-charge layers due to air breakdown and negative surface-charge layers caused by ohmic relaxation or by dipole effects are present on some samples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sensitivity stability of electret transducers
abstract: Based on equations derived previously, the authors develop a method for determining the parameters of an electret transducer. With the approach described, it is possible to implement a nondestructive method for finding the parameters of an electret transducer. A formula for electret microphone sensitivity can then be used to predict the sensitivity variation versus variation parameters with time (i.e., by discharging an electret and simultaneous weakening of membrane tension).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of charge density and location of the charge centroid in electrets with semiconducting substrates
abstract: A novel method for determining the amount and the mean spatial depth of charges in electret-semiconductor systems is presented. It consists of two nondestructive measurements, from which the internal and external electric fields can be calculated independently. First, the surface potential at the electret-air interface is measured by an electrostatic voltmeter. Secondly, using a contacting front electrode, a metal insulator semiconductor structure is formed, on which capacitance or conductance voltage measurements are carried out. With these, one obtains the surface potential at the electret-semiconductor interface. The charge centroid and the charge density can now be calculated. Application of the method to 1- mu m SiO/sub 2/ electrets on silicon substrates showed that the charge centroid and the charge density could be varied with an annealing procedure before charging.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Phase transition in corona charged alpha -PVDF samples in dry air
abstract: The constant current corona triode has been used to charge and monitor the surface potential buildup of alpha -PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride) samples. Under dry conditions it is possible to pole the samples to sufficiently high electric fields so as to cause a phase change from the nonpolar alpha form to the polar alpha /sub p/ form. This phase transition is identified in the surface potential buildup by a plateau in which dipole orientation occurs, and can also be confirmed by X-ray diffractograms. A tentative theoretical model which takes into account ferroelectric polarization is developed to explain quantitatively the experimental results obtained for alpha /sub p/-PVDF.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of the air humidity on the corona polarization of beta -PVDF films
abstract: The corona triode making it possible to charge polymeric foils with a constant current has proved to be a powerful method for studying charge storage and transport. For ferroelectric polymers it allows one to determine the coercive field and the remanent polarization. A special version of such a triode was developed for poling samples in a controlled atmosphere. The results show that for beta -PVDF (polyvinylidenefluoride) samples the surface potential build-up is dependent on the air humidity. For a dry air atmosphere, the polarization clearly shows the ferroelectric behavior of the PVDF sample. A tentative explanation for the saturation of the potential build-up dependence on the humidity takes into account the increase in conductivity due to the water in the bulk of the polymer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The trapping of electrons in polystyrene
abstract: The trapping of electrons in localized states in polystyrene has been studied by means of an electron beam technique. A 2.2 kV beam is used to inject a short pulse of charge into the free surface of a thin film of the polymer, and a second electron beam monitors the surface potential of the film. The surface potential is related to trapped charge density and to the depth of charge penetration. Defining a trapping parameter alpha (=1/ mu tau E), one can relate the incremental buildup of surface potential to the injected charge density and carrier range. The release of electrons from traps is analyzed in terms of a time and temperature dependent demarcation energy. The time dependence of charge decay is related to the energy distribution of traps in the polymer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation of the EPDM copolymer using the pressure wave propagation method
abstract: The authors report the use of the pressure wave propagation (PWP) method to investigate the electrical properties of EPDM (ethylene-propylene copolymer) filled with different percentages of alumina. First the authors determine the velocity, attenuation, and dispersion of the pressure wave pulse for varying percentages of the filler. Then they discuss the charge injection process, from which it is concluded that charge injection is stronger when the content of alumina filler is increased.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Xerographic depletion discharge versus injection for modelling the surface potential decay in insulators
abstract: The surface potential dark decay after corona charging of inorganic amorphous semiconductors (a-Se, a-Se/sub 1-x/Te/sub x/, a-As/sub 2/Se/sub 3/) and organic polymers (high-density polyethylene, P(AN-MA)) follows in many cases a power-law time dependence with different exponents in two distinct time domains separated by a characteristic time. A careful analysis of experimental data from the literature and original measurements shows, however, that the seemingly identical phenomenology exhibits very different dependences of empirical parameters on field strength and temperature. Is is suggested that a consistent physical interpretation of the measurements is achievable in the case of inorganic semiconductors under the assumption of thermal generation and in the case of polymers with injection of charge carriers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Silicon subminiature microphones with organic piezoelectric layers: fabrication and acoustical behaviour
abstract: A silicon subminiature microphone, based on the piezoelectric effect of organic films such as aromatic polyurea, PVDF, and P(VDF/TrFE) (polyvinylidene fluoride/trifluoroethylene) is proposed. The acoustical sensor is fabricated using a slightly modified integrated circuit technology process and a standard micromechanical fabrication procedure. The main production steps of this 'hybrid' sensor are described, including the fabrication of the mechanical part of the sensor, the deposition or spin coating of the films, and the poling of the polymer layers. Measurements of the transverse piezoelectric charge constant d/sub 31/ and results of this sensitivity to airborne sound of the aromatic polyurea microphones are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Space charge and polarization in PETP at different temperatures
abstract: PETP (polyethyleneterephthalate) samples were poled at constant voltage and at different temperatures. Charge injection and orientation of dipoles as a function of the poling time at temperatures above 60 degrees C were measured with the PPS method under short circuit conditions. At room temperature the temporal injection and migration of space charges were observed. After long poling times a characteristic distribution of charges was observed. For temperatures above 60 degrees C, a strong additional orientation of dipoles in the field direction was observed. In cooling down to room temperature under field the dipoles remained oriented with strong piezoelectricity of the film. A few days later the injected space charges in excess of dipole compensation vanished. Most of the dipoles remained oriented for several months.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direct observation of space charge evolution in e-irradiated Kapton films
abstract: The pressure wave propagation method has been applied to analyze the evolution of the space charge in e-irradiated Kapton H films. The 125 mu m thick films are irradiated in a vacuum chamber with a monoenergetic electron beam in the 10-50 keV energy range. The method allows the direct observation of the depth of penetration of electrons. First results on Kapton are presented. The space charge evolution in the irradiation and nonirradiated regions is studied during and after the irradiation process. Trapped electrons drift in the nonirradiated zone towards the electrode interface where they build up. Positive charges appear in the bulk of the sample both in the irradiated and nonirradiated regions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear conductive spectra of ion-conducting polymers
abstract: An ion-conducting polymer, tetraethylene oxide-organosiloxane (TEOS) copolymer, was synthesized and the linear and nonlinear complex conductivities were measured as a function of frequency. Observed spectra were reproduced by taking into account the interfacial and electrode polarizations. The most important findings are the very large dielectric relaxation strength and the very long hopping distance in noncrystalline ion-conductivity polymers. The large relaxation strength suggests that the TEOS Li/sup -/ comprises an inhomogeneous system consisting of highly conductive and less conductive regions. It is speculated that such inhomogeneity governs the conduction mechanisms of the ionic conductor and results in a very long hopping distance. A combination of linear and nonlinear DC conductivities leads to a hopping distance of 200 nm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristics of a radiation-charged electret dosimeter
abstract: The radiation-charged electret ionization-chamber uses an electret formed in situ by applying a bias voltage to the chamber electrodes while the chamber is being irradiated with X-rays. An electrometer permits measurement of the charge on the electret surface before and after the use of the chamber as a dosimeter. The authors present measurements of dosimeter range, sensitivity, and energy dependence as functions of bias potential, electrode separation, guard-ring size, and various materials. Reproducibility permits detection as low as 55 mu Gys with range up to 100's of cGys depending on the design of the chamber, with charge retention properties similar to those of electrets formed from corona discharge.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pressure effect on the space charge in low density polyethylene (LDPE)
abstract: The electrical conductivity of LDPE films was studied with temperature (30 degrees C to 75 degrees C), electrical field (6.3 to 22.5 MV/m), and pressure (1 to 850 bar). An anomalous discharge current was observed in the transient state after the application of a DC field, for example, above 15.3 Mv/m for 55 degrees C. The anomalous current, depending on these parameters, was attributed to the existence of a space charge in the polymer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Chemical surface treatment of PMMA electrets
abstract: The surface of PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate) electrets was treated by hexamethyl disilazane until a stable retention of charges was achieved. Adopting suitable organic reagents and treated conditions, the surface treatment of polar polymers will be able to modify the stability of electret charge retention.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pyroelectric properties of a new composite material-PVDF-TGS film
abstract: The dielectric content and pyroelectric coefficient of PVDF-TGS (polyvinylidene fluoride-triglycine sulfate) film have been investigated. Its figure of merit M(P/ in ) was calculated. This composite film has already been used to make IR detectors. All the results obtained have shown that PVDF-TGS composite is a prospective important pyroelectric material.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Structural orientation and electric polarization of polymers in stationary magnetic fields
abstract: Magnetic fields (MFs) of 100 to 500 kA/m were found to order magnetoanisotropic structural units in nonpolar polymer melts, e.g., polyethylene (PE). A temperature range and a threshold intensity of MF were observed when PE melt was partially ordered, i.e., when it was in a quasi-liquid-crystalline state. It is believed that thermomagnetic treatment of polymers in MFs can result in electrical polarization and formation of magnetoelectrets. A relationship is believed to exist between the polarization processes and the orientation of magnetoanisotropic macromolecules and aggregates in MFs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electron-beam charging of plasma-coated spacecraft dielectrics
abstract: Research results are described on the charge accumulation and arc discharging of coated dielectric sheets exposed to a 20-keV electron beam. The dielectric sheet substrates are Kapton and Mylar, and the coatings are plasma-deposited amorphous hydrogenated silicon (a-Si:H), silicon nitride (P-SiN), and silicon dioxide (P-SiO/sub 2/). Arc discharges are characterized by their current pulse shape and by their appearance as recorded using a CCD (charge coupled device) camera. Results indicate that P-SiO/sub 2/ and P-SiN coatings on Kapton prevent discharge occurrence. Other coating-substrate combinations do not prevent discharges but do modify them.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Charge distribution in Teflon FEP negatively corona-charged to high potentials
abstract: The charge distribution in negatively corona-charged Teflon FEP films was investigated with the laser-induced pressure-pulse method. The 12.7 mu m and 25.4 mu m samples were charged to potentials up to -2500 V and -4500 V, respectively, and thereafter stored at room temperature. Measurements of the charge distribution were taken at time intervals ranging from 1 minute to several days after charging. The results indicated that the corona charge is initially trapped at the surface of the samples. A negative bulk charge, which is distributed over the entire volume and has a density of approximately 10/sup 13//cm/sup 3/, is found for samples kept at the highest voltages for periods of the order of hours. The findings suggest that in highly charged samples intrinsic holes drift to the charged surface, leading to a depletion of holes and thus to the observed negative bulk charge.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polarization effects in high density polyethylene containing an antioxidant
abstract: The method of thermally stimulated discharge currents is used to study trapped charge in high-density polyethylene containing an antioxidant. The charge stability increases when polarization temperature increases. If the sample is not heated during the TSDC experiment to the melting point, a large current is released during the cooling of the sample. The currents released in the TSDC experiments are still very large. From the current shape and activation energy value for different annealing times, it was concluded that during cooling and annealing part of the charge moves from deeper traps toward the shallow traps. If the stored charge is neither too big nor too small the TSDC spectrum is complex and is sensitive to all physical transformations in the sample.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Space charge limited currents in spherulitic polypropylene
abstract: Space-charge-limited currents were observed in spherulitic polypropylene films containing large spherulites which are two-dimensionally grown. The number of charge-trapping sites N/sub t/ and the mobility mu were estimated to be of the orders of 10/sup 14/ (cm/sup -3/) and 10/sup -9/ (cm/sup 2/-V/sup -1/-s/sup -1/), respectively. It was also found that N/sub t/ decreased with increasing mean diameter R of spherulites in the sample, while mu increased with R.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bulk water effect on charge current on PVDF
abstract: An evanescent transient current in step-voltage measurements carried out with alpha -PVDF samples has been detected. This effect is strongly dependent on the moisture of the environment. Experimental results have indicated that this transient current is generated by the ionic dissociation of the absorbed water molecules by the bulk of the sample.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polarization built-up during constant current corona charging of PVDF
abstract: From time dependences of the electret potential under different constant charging currents, as well as from the I-V characteristics and TSP (thermally stimulated polarization) curves, it is found that the process of polarization build-up in PVDF (polyvinylidenefluoride) consists of three stages. Strong polarization nucleates at the beginning of the second stage and its further growth is controlled by a process similar to the propagation of domain walls in ferroelectrics. The following data were obtained experimentally: a coercive field of 48 MV/m, a saturated polarization of 58 mC/m/sup 2/, and an effective mobility of charge carriers of 10/sup -8/ m/sup 2//(V-s).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the equivalence of the mechanisms governing switching and hysteresis phenomena
abstract: The nucleation and growth model, which is usually applied to switching phenomena, is adapted for explaining surface potential measurements on the P(VDF-TrFE) (polyvinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) copolymer obtained in a constant current corona triode. It is shown that the growth is one-dimensional and that the nucleation rate is unimportant, probably because surface potential measurements take much longer than the switching ones. The surface potential data can therefore be accounted for by a growth model in which the velocity of growth varies exponentially with the electric field. Since hysteresis loops can be obtained from surface potential measurements, it is suggested that similar mechanisms can be used when treating switching and hysteresis phenomena, provided that account is taken of the difference in the time scale of the measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Poling of thin films of aromatic polyurea during polymerization and crystallization
abstract: Piezoelectricity and pyroelectricity were observed in poled films of aromatic polyurea less than 1 mu m thick, which were synthesized by concurrent deposition of a diamine monomer and a diisocyanate monomer in vacuum. The films are poled by applying an electric field of 100 MV/m at 200 degrees C. X-ray diffraction measurements show that crystallization takes place at about 160 degrees C. The infrared absorption due to C=O stretch vibration in the isocyanate groups at the chain ends disappears after heat treatment. It is concluded that the alignment of urea dipoles takes place during polymerization and crystallization. Stable residual polarization produces the piezoelectric and pyroelectric activities persistent up to 200 degrees C.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Charging temperature effect for corona charged Teflon FEP electret
abstract: The effect of charging temperature on charge storage of corona charged Teflon FEP (fluoroethylene propylene) electret is investigated. When the sample is negatively charged at elevated temperatures, a nonuniform charge distribution with the charge concentration in the near-surface that is greater than in the bulk is confirmed with the laser-induced pressure pulse method. By contrast, a uniform charge distribution throughout the bulk of the material is attainable so long as the sample is positively corona charged above 90 degrees C. According to the charge distribution and the trap structure, analysis shows that the charging temperature plays an important role in the charge stability for the Teflon FEP electret.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of the interface/interphase on polarization phenomena in model composites
abstract: Thermally stimulated current (TSC) spectroscopy has been applied to the study of interface/interphase in model composites. Three DGEBA-DDA matrix samples have been analyzed: matrix, matrix+silane treated beads, and matrix+elastomer coated beads. Below room temperature, two polarization phenomena are observed in all samples. The relaxation mode associated with the dielectric manifestation of the glass transition of the elastomeric interlayer has also been observed. Above room temperature, the TSC spectra show the existence of a complex relaxation mode. Analysis of the relaxation times shows compensation phenomena with parameters characteristic of the interface/interphase.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of the measurement of polarization distributions by the LIMM and PWP methods
abstract: Two different methods of measurement of polarization distributions in piezoelectric materials, the LIMM (laser intensity modulation method) and the PWP (pressure wave propagation) methods, are compared. After briefly describing the two techniques, the authors report measurements made on different PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride) samples, one with a symmetric and the other with an antisymmetric structure. Although the LIMM method responds to diffusion of heat and the PWP method to the propagation of a pressure wave, the direct observation of the raw data gives in both cases the same information concerning the symmetry of the polarization distribution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pyroelectric and piezoelectric studies on BaTiO/sub 3/: silica glass composites
abstract: BaTiO/sub 3/:silica-glass composites were prepared in different weight ratios and their dielectric constant was studied over a wide temperature and frequency range. The results indicated that with increasing amounts of silica the dielectric constant of the composite goes on decreasing, while their Curie temperature increases. Pyroelectric current and charge field hysteresis effects were also studied in these composites. It was observed that the pyroelectric coefficient decreases from 238 mu C/m/sup 2/K to 200 mu C/m/sup 2/K as the percentage of glass in the composite is increased. The piezocoefficient d/sub 33/ also shows a decrease with increasing glass percentage but the piezovoltage coefficient peaks at 1% glass content.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The windowing polarization technique and its possibilities in the study of conduction mechanisms in polymers
abstract: It can be observed in electrets of PET-A, using the windowing polarization technique and TSC (thermally stimulated current) spectroscopy, that the polar peak ( alpha ) and the peak of charge ( rho ) show a maximum polarization at a certain temperature of polarization T/sub p/=T/sub po/. The peak alpha , for T/sub p/>T/sub po/, shows maxima at a temperature (T/sub m/) that is constant versus T/sub p/ as long as P=f(1/T/sub p/) is a linear function, and it is possible to calculate its effective energy of activation above the T/sub po/. The peak rho , for T/sub p/>T/sub po/, results in a plot of P=f(1/T/sub p/) that is not linear, whereas T/sub m/=f(T/sub p/) is a linear and increasing function. The results obtained from PVC (polyvinyl chloride) and PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate) are compared and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High electric fields in DC poled glasses examined with the LIPP technique
abstract: The depletion layer generated in DC poled soda-lime glasses was investigated using the LIPP (laser-induced pressure pulse) technique. The electric condition prevailing in the depletion layer was studied, using samples with two different kinds of electrodes. The results are interpreted taking advantage of the chemical surface analysis already carried out.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamics of poling PVDF between 250 degrees C and 120 degrees C
abstract: PVDF films with high beta -content are poled in an electric field of 60 MV/m at temperatures between 25 degrees C and 120 degrees C. At 25 degrees C the alignment of dipoles takes place in a central poling zone during several hours of poling. When the temperature is increased to 120 degrees C the poling time necessary to align the dipoles in this narrow zone is reduced to several seconds. In addition, at temperatures higher than 90 degrees C and increased poling times the central poling zone first increases but later decreases in its dielectric displacement. Simultaneously in a 10 mu m regime adjoining the positive electrode a secondary displacement zone starts to grow. The strong reduction of this peak under short circuit conditions indicates hetero-charge accumulation in front of an anode.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nature of new tau -peak in thermally stimulated current spectra of PET electrets
abstract: A new current peak, the tau -peak, whose appearance temperature is higher than that of the rho -peak, is found from TSC (thermally stimulated current) spectra of PET (polyethylene terephthalate) electrets which possess a higher degree of planar orientation and a larger crystallinity (>30%) or are gamma -irradiated by a larger dose (>200 Mrad). The nature of the tau -peak is still the detrapping of trapped charge carriers, but the trap depth represented by the tau -peak is deeper and the ability of the trapping charge carriers is better as compared with that of the rho -peak.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of the physical ageing on electrical conductivity and dielectric measurements of amorphous poly(ethylene terephthalate)
abstract: Electrical conductivity and dielectric relaxation measurements have been carried out during the physical ageing of amorphous poly(ethylene terephthalate) in the range of ageing temperatures T/sub a/ between 50 and 70 degrees C and ageing times t/sub a/ between 10 min and 72 h. Both the intensity of the current and the imaginary part of the complex dielectric permittivity in " (or dissipation factor tan delta ) decrease with t/sub a/, at T/sub a/ constant, as a consequence of the structural relaxation of the material, reaching a constant value in a time which depends on the temperature. As T/sub a/ increases, the decay of the intensity and in " (or tan delta ) increases as a consequence of the greater extension of the relaxation which shows a maximum in the interval 60-65 degrees C for t/sub a/>or=6 h.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric behavior of 0-3 type piezoelectric composites
abstract: Dielectric absorption and thermally stimulated current measurements were performed for PPN-P(VDF/TFE) (polyvinylidene fluoride/tetrafluoroethylene) composites obtained by hot-pressing of PPN ceramic and PVDF powder. Dielectric dispersion was observed in the composites with the maximum of absorption in the range of approximately 10 MHz at room temperature. The dispersion is characterized by a broad relaxation-time distribution. Electrical transport in the composite at temperatures below approximately 370 K is influenced by relaxation processes of the polymer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hydration properties of PHEA/Kevlar composites studied by dielectric, DSC and sorption isotherm measurements
abstract: The authors present a detailed study of the dielectric properties of poly(hydroxyethyl acrylate) (PHEA) and PHEA/Kevlar composites by means of the thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) method, partial heating, and thermal sampling techniques in a wide range of temperatures and water contents. The measurements make it possible to investigate the influence of moisture on the different relaxation mechanisms and the different binding modes of water. Additional information is obtained from differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and sorption isotherm measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear dielectric investigation of ferroelectric liquid crystals
abstract: The dynamical characteristics of ferroelectric liquid crystals were investigated by means of nonlinear dielectric measurements such as D-E hysteresis, in -E hysteresis loop, nonlinear relaxation spectra, and bias-field-dependent linear relaxation spectra. Molecular motions considered were the thermally activated Goldstone mode and the field-induced switching mode. The Goldstone mode is highly suppressed by the switching mode due to loss of helical structure. Although they arise from a common elementary process related to the azimuth angle, they are distinguished by the difference in nonlinear nature that the saturated polarization of the former remains one half that of the latter. This implies that there exists a potential barrier in the midway of large-amplitude Goldstone mode fluctuations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Annealing effects in TSD-spectra of SiO/sub 2/ electrets
abstract: Electron-beam or corona charged SiO/sub 2/ electrets were investigated by measuring open-circuit TSD-currents in the temperature range between 20 degrees C and 500 degrees C. It was found that annealing of the samples before charging shifts or even generates peaks in the TSD-spectrum. Therefore annealing time and temperature dependence were investigated intensively. The results are important for the production of very stable SiO/sub 2/ electrets and give information about the charge storage mechanism in such electrets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Corona charging of electrets: models and results
abstract: Summary form only given. Some results on corona charging of electrets are discussed. Particular attention is given to free space charge, deep fast trapping, the Arkhipov-Rudenko-Sessler model, and the simple Von Seggern-Wang model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated discharge and heat pulse responses of UV irradiated corona Teflon FEP films
abstract: One-side metallized negatively-corona-charged UV-irradiated Teflon FEP films show changes in their TSD (thermally stimulated discharge) curves as compared with those of nonirradiated samples. They are practically discharged after the first TSD process, indicating that UV (ultraviolet) irradiation makes the contact able to inject positive charge. Heat pulse records confirm positive injection from a UV-irradiation contact. UV-irradiated positively charged films have a residual potential larger than the unirradiated one and also show peak shifts in their TSD thermograms. Results are shown for different metallic contacts.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated currents in holmium oxide-based thin-film capacitors
abstract: Results of experimental examinations of vacuum-evaporated aluminum/holmium oxide/aluminum thin-film thermoelectrets by the method of thermally stimulated currents are presented. All measurements were carried out in the temperature region from 297 K to 500 K with the help of an automated microcomputer-based system. The TSD (thermally stimulated depolarization current) and TSP (thermally stimulated polarization current) curves obtained under different measurement conditions exhibit only a single peak for the temperatures between 380 K and 406 K. The trapping levels with the activation energy of 0.5-0.7 eV are responsible for the observed results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Corona-triode characteristics: on effects possibly caused by the electronic component
abstract: The plate current for negative corona in a corona triode is observed to become positive and saturate at a value I/sub s/ when the grid-to-plate distance is less than 15 mm and the grid is biased positively. The saturation current, I/sub s/, is strongly dependent on the point-to-grid distance, which appears to indicate that the current is linked to those high energy hot electrons which survive attachment and are capable of ionizing molecules below the grid. Also investigated are the dependence of the saturation current on a few parameters and the current density distribution over the plate area. The relevance to the effects of corona treatment on the surface charge decay of polymer samples is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of electric field on properties of 0-3 fine composites with PbTiO/sub 3/ ultrafine powders
abstract: PbTiO/sub 3/ (PT) polar ultrafine powders derived from the sol-gel process were dispersed in liquid and epoxy matrices. The change of scattered light, transmitted light, optical absorption, and refractive index by these PT ultrafine powders dispersed in liquid and epoxy matrices was investigated in detail. The field-induced light scattering is about 50%, while transmitted light can be increased by 100% with increase of external field applied on the PT suspension. The optical absorption edge is shifted from 2.95 eV to 2.76 eV in fine PT composites. The change of refractive index is about 10/sup -4/ in order of PT suspension. All experimental results indicate that there is a strong interaction between PT particles and dispersed systems under external AC and DC electric field. All optical properties can be modified by applying an electric field on composites.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stability of polytetrafluorethylene electrets in dependence on material structure
abstract: Electret properties of nonoriented polytetrafluoroethylene (PTEE) films of different molecular structure were investigated. The structure was modified by using different heat-treatment conditions, the changes in structure being determined by infrared spectroscopy and wide-angle X-ray diffraction methods. The stability of negatively charged electrets was found to decrease with the decrease of crystallinity, longitudinal and transverse crystallite sizes, and the increase of the part of conformation defects. In a far-infrared region, absorption bands were associated with the part and regularity of folded regions in the crystal which are supposedly responsible for the formation of shallow traps for negative charges. The kinetics of the isothermal discharge of positively charged electrets appeared to be less sensitive for the structural modification of films. Positive charge localization either in the paracrystal phase regions or on the surface states is assumed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and properties of a pyroelectric microcalorimeter
abstract: A pyroelectric calorimeter consists of a pyroelectric sensor with the sample directly deposited onto one of the electrodes of the sensor. The arrangement is heated by the absorption of intensity modulated radiation at the other electrode of the pyroelectric sensor. In the case of a homogeneously poled pyroelectric sensor, the quotient of the pyroelectric current, gained at modulation frequencies omega below and above omega =2D/d/sup 2/, with D the thermal diffusivity and d the thickness of the pyroelectric sensor material, directly yields the quotient of the heat capacity of the pyroelectric materials and the sample. Experimental results are shown with a 30 mu m thick LiTaO/sub 3/ crystal and 25 mu m and 9 mu m thick PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride) films as calorimeter materials, and with 25 mu m thick Ag-foils and a 1.25 mu m thick polyglutamate Langmuir-Blodgett film.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Positive electret substrates enhance neuroblastoma process outgrowth
abstract: FEP (fluorinated ethylene propylene) electret substrates provide a means of investigating the biological response of neuronal cells contacting a charged surface. Mouse neuroblastoma cells were placed on positive, negative, and uncharged FEP substrates, and were assessed for process outgrowth. Significantly more cells sent out neurite processes on positive substrates as compared to negative and uncharged substrates. Electron spectroscopy for chemical analysis, contact angle analysis, and scanning electron microscopy revealed no surface chemical or morphological distinction between charged and uncharged substrates. This study demonstrates that a positively charged surface induces greater neuronal outgrowth than a negatively charged or uncharged surface.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On formation of electret state during friction of polymers
abstract: The electret effect resulting from friction of polymers was investigated. It is argued that the electret state in nonpolar polymers can be caused by injection processes. For friction of polar polymers dipole polarization resulting from the orientation of dipole groups was shown to be of importance. Two factors, mechanical and electrostatic, were found to be responsible for the polarization during friction of polymers. A mechanism is suggested to explain the formation of the electret state in polymers during frictional interaction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Anomalous discharge process in copolymers of vinylidene fluoride
abstract: Anomalous discharge behavior involving the occurrence of a current peak in the isothermal discharge process has been observed for vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene (VDF/TFE) copolymers in the paraelectric phase. The current peak was found for VDF/TFE copolymer with high TFE content in the paraelectric and also for VDF/HFP (hexafluoropropylene) copolymer with 2 mol.% HFP taking structure of the form 11 PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride). The anomalous behavior is connected with retarded migration or diffusion of ionic charge bound with molecular dipoles in crystalline regions. The VDF group or the VDF sequence in the copolymer possibly plays an important role in trapping or restraining ions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effects of irradiation dose rate and thermal aging on changes in the properties of elastomeric materials (EPR-CSPE) for cable insulation and sheathing
abstract: In order to estimate cable service life in PWR plants, a research program has been established and performed on EPR/CSPE (ethylene-propylene rubber/chlorosulfonated polyethylene) LOCA (loss-of-coolant accident) cables based on a study of the dose and dose rate effects and the temperature. The authors present the results of accelerated tests and physicochemical studies (IR, mechanical properties, oxidation (EPR), and chlorine (CSPE) stabilities) carried out to characterize the degree of degradation of the materials. EPR seems to be sensitive to the dose rate effect with oxidation at low dose rate and crosslinking at high dose rate. CSPE is degraded by crosslinking. For both EPR and CSPE, the activation energy of oxidation stability and dehydrochlorination, respectively, have been evaluated as a function of the thermal aging.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of space charge effects on electrical properties of polymers by direct probing
abstract: Direct and quantitative probing of space charge was carried out to study the effects of space charge on the dielectric breakdown of polymeric insulating materials. In poly-p-phenylene sulfide, in which dielectric-breakdown characteristics were explained in terms of space-charge formation, positive homo space charge was observed. The amount and the depth of space charge detected agreed well with those assumed from the breakdown characteristics. Similar results were also obtained for oxidized PE (polyethylene), where prominent electron injection and negative-homo-space-charge formation took place.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High field conduction and space charge formation in ethylene-styrene copolymers
abstract: High field conduction and space charge formation in low-density polyethylene and ethylene-styrene copolymers were studied by measuring DC conduction and thermal pulse current at various temperatures. Conduction current is considered to be dominated by traps due to benzene rings introduced into copolymers. At room temperature, injected electrons and holes seem to be trapped near the cathode and anode, respectively. At 50 degrees C, electrons are considered to be transported by overcoming the effect of traps, and holes seem to become mobile at 90 degrees C. The number of mobile carriers is a function of styrene content and temperature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Radiation-induced conductivity in electron-beam irradiated insulating polymer films
abstract: The radiation-induced conductivity (RIC) in PP (polypropylene), PETP (polyethyleneterephthalate), and PI (polyimide) due to electron-beam irradiation is measured with an external bias method and, in the case of PP, also with a short-circuit method, as a function of dose rate and time of irradiation or total dose. The results substantiate the power-law dependence of the RIC on dose rate in all cases but indicate that the dependence on time is different for the materials under investigation. In addition, the delayed radiation-induced conductivity (DRIC) is determined. The DRIC shows a hyperbolic time dependence with different exponents for the different materials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated depolarization currents of polymers: a new analysis and significance of the compensation law
abstract: The model introduced by K.L. Ngai to predict the relaxation behavior of condensed matter is used to derive the expression of thermally stimulated depolarization currents. A test to probe a possible common origin of two relaxation processes is suggested. Furthermore, physical aging is qualitatively taken into account. The compensation law then appears as a consequence of the variation with T of the stretching index n of the model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of X- and gamma-irradiation on selected electrical properties of polyethylene terephthalate films
abstract: Thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSD) and measurements of permittivity, loss factor, and DC conductivity on X-ray and gamma-irradiated polyethylene terephthalate (PETP) films were investigated. The commercial ESTROFOL PETP film, 125 mu m thick, was investigated. Samples were X- and gamma-irradiated with three different doses in different gaseous environments (air and N/sub 2/) and the electrical properties were measured as a function of time. Applying partial heating techniques, a distribution of activation energies of relaxation processes, being responsible for varies as and rho peaks, was found.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pyroelectric and piezoelectric properties of sol-gel derived BaTiO/sub 3/-polymer composites
abstract: BaTiO/sub 3/ was prepared using the sol gel process. Dried gel was crushed and fired at different temperature from 400 degrees C to 800 degrees C. Composites were prepared in 0-3 connectivity using BaTiO/sub 3/ fired at different temperatures and PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride). Hysteresis, dielectric-constant, and pyroelectric-current measurements were carried out on these samples. Comparison of these results with those of the solid-solution-dried BaTiO/sub 3/ revealed significant improvement in their properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric relaxation studies in liquid crystal polymers by thermally stimulated depolarization current method
abstract: The thermally stimulated depolarization current method and the thermally stimulated polarization current method have been used for the study of the star poly ( gamma -stearyl- alpha , L-glutamate) polymer. The beta peak appears around -88 degrees C and is determined by side-dipole moments. Three other peaks appear: alpha /sub 1/, alpha /sub 1/', and alpha /sub 2/. The activation energy was determined for beta and alpha /sub 2/ peaks for different heating rates. A good correlation between heating rate and T/sub m//sup 2/ was found. The position of the alpha /sub 2/ peak is very close to that determined by DSC thermograms. The alpha /sub 1/ and alpha /sub 1/' peaks are strongly influenced by the thermal treatment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical and nonlinear optical properties of polydiacetylene Langmuir-Blodgett film
abstract: The electrical and optical properties of polydiacetylene (10, 12-pentacosa-diynoic acid) films deposited by using the Langmuir-Blodgett technique and then polymerized were studied. A change in electrical conduction with polymerization suggested the contribution of the conjugated system as hopping centers. Third harmonic generation was observed, and a change in third order susceptibility chi /sup (3)/ is discussed in connection with structural change associated with polymerization, annealing, and so on. The third-harmonic generation is mainly due to the blue form and the structure responsible for the optical absorption around 700 nm did not contribute much to the third-harmonic generation. Steric constraints due to this structure may suppress the polymerization and extension of a conjugate system. Deposition of multilayers seems to increase structural defects and hinder the progress of polymerization. The conjugated system due to polymerization may act as additional hopping centers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric measurements and X-ray investigations on the phase transitions of poly (vinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene) copolymers
abstract: Paraelectric-to-ferroelectric phase transition has been observed under low electrical stresses in vinylidenefluoride-hexafluoropropylene (VDF-HFP) copolymers with 15% HFP molar content. This phase transition, detected by thermodepolarization processes and differential scanning calorimetry techniques, is confirmed in the present work by X-ray and dielectric measurements. These results showed the structural evolution of the copolymer from the alpha nonpolar to the delta polar configuration under electrical stress of 0.5 MV/cm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermal depolarization of PVDF: anomaly at 180 degrees C
abstract: PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride) samples with high beta -content (80%), prepolarized at room temperature, were heated to higher temperatures. The polarization was measured first under open circuit conditions at the high temperature and then cooling down again to room temperature. For elevated temperatures up to 175 degrees C the polarization is reduced to 2% of the original value, yet covers roughly to 8% of the original value after cooling down again to room temperature. In contrast, when heating up the films to 180 degrees C a significantly different behavior was observed: in cooling down to room temperature the polarization returns from about 1% at 180 degrees C to about 40% of the original prepolarized value.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of Golay codes to biomedical transducers for non-invasive measurement
abstract: Golay codes have been combined with an experimental piezoelectric transducer in a water bath. It is shown that signal-to-noise-ratio improvements resulting from this are greatest when the input signal-to-noise ratio is greater than unity and the target is obscured by clutter. Further, it is shown that this system can be used to send multiple codes, with code identification after detection, to extend the range-velocity limit in medical Doppler systems. The simple processing involved gives significant improvement in noise performance for no increase in bandwidth against standard maximal length pseudo-random binary systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Water induced bioelectret state in aminoacidic homopolymers
abstract: In order to attribute each peak of the complex TSDC (thermally stimulated depolarization current) lysozyme spectrum to a water-induced polarization process occurring at a given polypeptide chain segment, the authors have measured and compared the TSDC and infrared absorption spectra of several aminoacidic synthetic homopolymers at different hydration levels. The A-band (135-160 K), present in all the homopolymers investigated, is due to water molecule reorientation around the peptide bond. The B-band ( approximately 215 K) is related to the relaxation of the side chains, whose mobility and reorientation parameters are affected by the hydration level.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Piezoelectricity of PVDF/PUE, PVDF/PMMA and PVDF/(PMMA+BaTiO/sub 3/) laminates
abstract: The author suggests the preparation of piezoelectric laminates using PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride) polymer film (a), polyester urethane elastomer (PUE) film (b), PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate) film (c), and (PMMA+BaTiO/sub 3/) composite film (d). Systems of three-layered structure of (aba), (aca), and (ada) have been made, and then conventional electrets based on these laminates have been prepared. The modification of internal layers in the systems leads to a change in their dielectric properties and also in the mechanical parameters which determine the piezoelectricity. The origins of piezoelectricity in these systems have been considered on the basis of TSD thermograms. It is shown that the initial piezoelectric constant d/sub 33/ is the highest for the PVDF-PMMA/BaTiO/sub 3/ system but the better piezoelectric stability can be obtained in electretized PVDF-PUE-PVDF laminate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ultrasonic piezoelectric transducer for biomedical applications
abstract: Ultrasonic piezoelectric transducers using PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride) films as active element and epoxy-tungsten composite as backing material were constructed. Simulated and experimentally obtained waveform responses and their power spectra of these transducers were compared. The correspondence of the waveform of the output of the transducers and of the power spectra of the simulation to those of the real transducers was fairly good.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Air electret disinfectant equipment
abstract: A description is given of an air electret filter (AEF), which is a type of air electret disinfectant equipment used for sterilizing sickrooms and operating rooms in a hospital. The apparatus is composed of electret PP film 30 mm wide, charged with a certain potential, and a corrugated aluminium foil 30 mm wide, 0.12 mm thick, rolled into a cylindrical filtering unit with a diameter of 58 mm. A number of these units were connected in series and assembled at the intake air tube or the exhaust pipe of an axial-flow fan to complete the apparatus. The AEF could be used for disinfecting sickrooms and operating rooms where the relevant bacteria killing rates were measured several times in order to determine the optimum conditions for disinfection after bacteria of given density had been sprinkled and the apparatus was operating for a certain time in the disinfecting cabinet.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Triboelectret state of polymer composites
abstract: The influence of rubbing conditions, and of concentration and dispersity of fillers on the parameters of the triboelectret state in polymeric coatings containing particular electroconducting (graphite, nickel) or dielectric (Teflon) fillers has been studied. The residual charge, the activation energy, and the temperature of the injected and polarized components of the triboelectret charge were found to increase with the sliding velocity, when small quantities (1 to 3%) of particulate metals were added; the effect of the residual charge in the coating and its relaxation time increased with filler dispersity. Similar effects were detected when higher quantities (4 to 15 vol.%) of dielectric fillers were added to the polymer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The electrical conductivity of very thin ferroelectric VDF-TrFE copolymer films
abstract: Very thin films (down to 40 nm) of vinylidenefluoride-trifluoroethylene (VDF-TrFE) copolymers were prepared by the spin-coating technique. A strong growth of the DC conductivity for increasing electric fields and decreasing film thicknesses is found. The temperature dependence of the conductivity follows an Arrhenius law with a clear change of the activation energy at 335 K for heating as well as cooling independent of the polarization.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of defects on dipolar reorientations of bioelectrets: hydroxyapatites
abstract: The natural filler of calcified tissues is nonstoichiometric apatites. These apatites are characterized by a Ca/P ratio larger or lower than 1.66 (stoichiometric ratio). Defects responsible for modification of the crystalline structure can be eliminated by annealing apatites at various temperatures. Hence, pretreated samples of nonstoichiometric apatites have been studied by thermally stimulated current (TSC) spectroscopy. Analysis of polarization phenomena shows the existence of either monophasic or biphasic structure. Information on localization and interaction of defects with structural ions is also provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated current study of amorphous phase of PPS
abstract: Polarization phenomena of unoriented and uniaxially oriented poly(p-phenylene sulfide) (PPS) have been investigated around the glass transition by thermally stimulated current (TSC) spectroscopy. The samples are characterized by a primary peak at 95 degrees C and a secondary peak at 75 degrees C for unoriented PPS and at 65 degrees C for uniaxially oriented PPS. According to differential scanning calorimetry data, they have been associated with the glass and subglass transition, respectively. The analysis of TSC relaxation modes reveals the presence of a higher local order in the amorphous phase of uniaxially oriented PPS than that of unoriented PPS. Moreover, molecular orientation has been found to increase the magnitude of the process of free volume diffusion, associated with conformational changes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Poly(vinylidene fluoride/trifluoroethylene) in pyroelectric single-element sensors
abstract: Copolymer thin films can be cast by coating at a thickness of 0.8 mu m to 2.5 mu m on solid silicon substrates as well as on unrestrained 800 nm thin SiO/sub 2//Si/sub 3/N/sub 3/ supporting membranes. Poling the P(VDF/TrFE) (poly(vinylidene fluoride/trifluoroethylene)) at about 140 V/ mu m a high spontaneous polarization can be obtained without any stretching process. Measurements of dielectric constant, dielectric losses, and pyroelectric coefficient confirm the ideal nature of these materials for pyroelectric detectors. Built-up single element detectors are distinguished by a high specific detectivity of 3.5*10/sup 8/ cm-Hz/sup 1/2//W at a frequency of 10 Hz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electric current due to excess charges in shorted dielectrics
abstract: The released current from a short-circuited dielectric which contains a space-charge cloud is calculated for a floating space charge distribution under the assumption that the leading edges of the space-charge cloud expand under the influence of a momentary electric field. At a given depth in the dielectric there is a zero field plane and the charge moves from the zero field plane to the two electrodes. The sum of displacement current and conduction current at x=0 and x=L is determined for two time periods. The model curves for released current for different activation energies and heating rates are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Escape depth of secondary electrons from electron-irradiated polymers
abstract: Measurements with polymers (Teflon and Mylar) have shown that the secondary electron emission from uncharged surfaces exceeds that from surfaces containing a positive surface charge. The reduced emission of charged surfaces is due to recombination between electrons undergoing emission and trapped holes within the charged layer. During the experiments the surface of the material was kept at a negative potential to assure that all secondary electrons reaching the surface from within the material are actually emitted. An analysis of the results yielded the maximum escape depth of the secondary electrons.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical charge transport in partial crystalline and amorphous polymer structures
abstract: The influence of static and dynamic structures on mechanisms of charge transport was investigated by means of isothermal current-voltage dependence for various polymeric materials systems based on poly(vinylchloride) and polyethylene. Poly(vinylchloride) was chemically dehydrochlorinated, thereby creating polyacetylene structures. These samples showed ten-decades-at-best higher conductivity than the precursor polymer in dependence on the concentration of double bonds. Electron spin resonance measurements supported the interpretation of electrical conduction by a hopping transport of electrons. The results obtained for dehydrochlorinated poly(vinylchloride) are compared with model mechanisms of charge transport in polyethylene and partial crystalline polyethylenes as borderline cases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neutron dosimetry using an electret albedo dosimeter
abstract: The method of albedo dosimetry can provide a measure of individual dose in stray neutron fields at nuclear power plants. Calculated and measured neutron sensitivities of a simple albedo dosimeter based on the utilization of the (n, alpha ) reaction on boron within the sensitive chamber volume of an electret ionization chamber are presented. It is noted that, for practical use in mixed neutron-gamma-fields, the area of the boron layer must be optimized in such a way that the sensitivities for photons and neutrons are equal to their effective dose equivalents. Then the total effective dose equivalent can be determined from the response of the ionization chamber.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Space charge accumulation in dielectrics irradiated with light charged particles
abstract: Accumulation of space charges in various solid dielectrics differing considerably by structure and physical properties as a result of irradiation by protons, deuterons, /sup 3//sub 2/He ions, and alpha -particles with 0.5 to 10 MeV per nucleon energy range and beam currents 10/sup -9/-5*10/sup -8/ A/cm/sup 2/ has been investigated. The total current density in a dielectric slab has been measured during and after irradiation. In a number of dielectrics the space charge distribution has been probed by radiation beam and acoustic pulse methods. Experimental investigations have shown that space charge distributions in various materials become similar once charged particle ranges exceed approximately 5 mu m.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric investigation of beta -cyclodextrin inclusion complexes as related to the guest molecule and the corresponding structure
abstract: The dielectric behavior of beta -CD (cyclodextrin) inclusion complexes with various organic guest molecules has been studied by the thermally stimulated depolarization current method in the temperature range 80-300 K and by conventional AC techniques in the frequency range 10 Hz-13 MHz. The results are discussed as compared with data obtained with beta -CD hydrates, as a function of their hydration content, and in relation to the guest molecule and the related structure of the system, as determined by X-ray diffraction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electric volume charging during radiation oxidation of polyethylene
abstract: The acoustic probe method was used for the study of the electric space charge dynamics in polyethylene irradiated by electrons. The samples investigated contained diffusion-introduced oxygen in volume. The results obtained point to the existence of a clear relation between the spatial distribution of the charge and the material oxidation degree. The major practical conclusion of the present study is the possibility of acting upon the process of volume charge formation under irradiation by changing the surrounding medium. In addition, direct control of the space charge distribution during irradiation may also serve as control of the radiation-chemical processes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The role of the persistent polarization in dielectric charging and relaxation of radioelectrets
abstract: Charge accumulation in polar dielectrics irradiated with charged particles is accompanied by formation of the slow component of the persistent polarization P/sub s/ which escapes registration by routine measurements of the permittivity in . Some ceramics and glasses with in <10 feature extremely high P/sub s/ on the order of 10/sup -7/ C/cm/sup 2/. The present analysis is based on a two-layer dielectric with a constant conductivity of the irradiated region while P/sub s/ is described by the Debye model. The appearance of the P/sub s/ substantially affects the build-up rate of the space charge in a dielectric.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A detailed TSD-study of the glass transition region of amorphous polymers
abstract: The glass-transition region of amorphous polyvinylacetate was investigated by means of thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDs). The thermal-sampling (TS) technique was applied to analyze the TSD alpha -peak in more detail. Structural relaxation which is the origin of physical aging affects the TSD alpha -peaks and the TS peaks of the glass-transition region strongly. This influence was taken into account by variation of the cooling and heating rates and by variation of annealing time at different temperatures near glass transition. Besides the collective processes of molecular motion, there are relaxation processes connected with local conformational changes which influence the low-temperature tail of the TSD alpha -peak.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristics of ethyl cellulose (EC): polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) blend electrets
abstract: Mechanisms of charge production and its persistence in one and both side vacuum-aluminized EC:PMMA blend foil thermoelectrets, prepared under different field and temperature conditions, have been analyzed using the short- and open-circuit thermally stimulated current (TSC) techniques. The results indicate the existence of heterocharge due to dipole orientation and ionic charge drift together with the injection of charge carriers from electrodes with their subsequent localization in surface and bulk traps. Various characteristics of both types of thermograms indicated the injection of charge carriers from electrodes during short-circuit TSC under high electric field created at the interface by the strong heterocharge.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transient currents in discharge mode in ethyl-cellulose: polymethyl methacrylate compounds
abstract: Transient currents were measured in discharge mode with ethyl-cellulose (EC):polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) compound samples as a function of charging field, temperature, and polymer weight ratio. These currents have been found to follow the Curie-von Schweidler law characterized with different slopes in short and long time regions. The isochronals have been found to give rise to a peak located at 80 degrees C. The corresponding activation energy values are found to increase with PMMA content and also with time of observation of discharge current.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution of space charge and its effect on micro-macro domain transition of PLZT 8/65/35
abstract: The space charge distribution of PLZT 8/65/35 was measured by the LIMM (laser intensity modulation method). It is concluded that space charge movement in PLZT 8/65/35 is very difficult at temperatures below 50 degrees C and is easy above 50 degrees C. A detailed discussion of the effect of space charge on the micro-macro domain transition is given. The large difference of dielectric anomalous temperature T/sub d/ measured on heating and cooling is mainly due to the effect of space charge; the abrupt disappearance of dielectric dispersion at T/sub d/ under DC bias is also due to the space charge effect.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Surface-charge distributions on radiation-charged electrets
abstract: The authors present measurements of surface-charge distributions on electrets formed isothermally by applying an external bias to an electret ionization chamber while irradiating with X-rays. Charge distributions were measured with an electrostatic voltmeter probe during the formation of the electret and at various times in the life of the electrets. Electrets were also stored over extended periods to observe charge retention characteristics. It was found that charge uniformity is unaffected by changes in charging bias, but is affected by separation of electrodes, and that charge life is similar to that observed on corona-charged electrets. Results of this study may also prove useful in electret dosimetry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Depolarization current at high temperature by migration of space charge
abstract: The author presents results obtained by a modified method of thermally stimulated depolarizing current of a polymer electret, i.e., after raising the temperature just under the liquidizing point of test material, one keeps temperature constant and continues measurement of current. There were peaks in a graph of current vs. time by depolarization of an electret of a polymer, e.g., polyethylene terephthalate. A sharp peak at the turning point of temperature and a broad peak which appears after the temperature is kept constant were found. These peaks are thought to be caused by migration of space charge. A simulation calculation is made.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic properties of phospholipid-water multilayers studied by dielectric relaxation spectroscopy
abstract: The authors report on thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) measurements in the temperature range 77-320 K on hydrated di-myristoil-phosphatidylcholine at different water contents up to 0.33 w/w, corresponding to approximately 18 water molecules per lipid molecule. The different relaxation mechanisms contributing to the complex thermograms are analyzed using special TSDC techniques, and the corresponding spectra of activation energies and entropy factors are determined. The results are discussed in terms of different structures of water in the context of multiphase model and head group mobilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Forced phase transition of ferroelectric polymers
abstract: The electrically forced phase transition of ferroelectric copolymers of vinylidene fluoride and trifluorethylene is considered. The ferroelectric phase transition temperature of nonpoled samples of the polymer, T/sub c/, rose due to application of an external bias electric field. On the other hand, in the case of poled samples, both rise and fall of T/sub c/, were observed. The experimental results are discussed in comparison with the effect of hydrostatic pressure on this phase transition.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modeling for the capture of charge by electrets-adjacency effect
abstract: It is shown that the response in relative charged terms of electrets subjected to gamma radiation from cobalt 60 is a function of the configuration (alone or with neighbor). Two geometrical configurations were studied, i.e., only one electret or four electrets glued on the back electrode of an electret chamber. The four-electret configurations has given for the response a more important gradient due to the adjacency effect than the one-electret configuration. This adjacency effect and the corresponding edge effect were used for xeroradiographic images.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Photoelectret characteristics of BaTiO/sub 3/ single crystal
